text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The 12-nation Southern African Development Community (SADC) has agreed to press the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) to allow trade in ivory from Africa, July Moyo, permanent secretary in Zimbabwe's ministry of environment and tourism, told the Herald. He said SADC -- which consists Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Lesotho, Namibia, Tanzania, South Africa, Swaziland, Zambia and Zimbabwe -- would speak with one voice at a CITES conference in Harare in June and hoped other countries would also support at least the partial lifting of a 1989 world ban in ivory trade.
- State-owned Air Zimbabwe's flights returned to normal on Sunday, a day after some 70 pilots and flight engineers ended a week-long strike for higher pay.
